name: Michel A. Khalaf

career.title: Regional SVP for Poland, Romania and the Baltics; President and CEO of Amplico Life
Deputy President and Chief Operating Officer
Regional President, Middle East, Africa and South Asia (MEASA); CEO of MetLife MEASA after the 2010 Alico acquisition
President, Europe, Middle East and Africa (EMEA)

background_rationale: After starting as an investment officer, he spent two decades running Alico and MetLife country and regional insurance businesses across Europe, the Middle East, Africa and Asia before leading MetLife's U.S. business.

notable.summary: Introduced the "Next Horizon" strategy, framed around focusing, simplifying and differentiating the company.
At MetLife's investor day, unveiled the five-year "New Frontier" plan targeting double-digit adjusted EPS growth, a 15-17% adjusted ROE and $25 billion in free cash flow.
Presenting New Frontier, Khalaf said MetLife operates in markets with "deep competitive moats and strong tailwinds" and is positioned to deliver growth with lower risk.
MetLife agreed to acquire asset manager PineBridge Investments for up to $1.2 billion, lifting MetLife Investment Management's assets to over $700 billion; the deal was reported completed in 2025.

personal_story.hook: Raised in Lebanon, Michel Khalaf joined Alico as an investment officer in 1989 and rose to run MetLife three decades later.
personal_story.summary: Khalaf was born in Lebanon in 1964, the son of Abbas Khalaf, who served as Lebanon's minister of economy and trade in the mid-1970s; his sister Roula Khalaf is editor of the Financial Times. He attended International College in Beirut, then earned an engineering degree and an MBA in finance at Syracuse University. He began his career as an investment officer at Alico, AIG's international life insurer, and spent the next two decades running its operations in markets from Egypt and Poland to the Philippines. When MetLife bought Alico in 2010 he joined MetLife, later leading its EMEA and U.S. businesses before becoming CEO in 2019.
